title: Composition-compatible affine-coordinate comparisons on K-flat labelled models
statement: Assume a derived category for the module sheaves on every scheme [def-pc-derived-category]. An affine coordinate consists of a commutative ring A, a scheme X [def-pc-scheme], an isomorphism Spec A ≅ X, a supplied derived equivalence d identified after localization with pushforward along this isomorphism, and a functor H from A-module cochain complexes identified naturally with termwise tilde, localization, and d. There exists a simultaneous family δ for every square σ_B ≫ p = Spec(φ) ≫ σ_A and every pair of acyclic-tensor K-flat complexes M,N [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. It is a natural isomorphism from scalar extension followed by H_B to H_A followed by Lp* [def-pc-derived-pullback], on the full induced category of the two labels. For three coordinates, ring maps φ,ψ,χ with χ=ψ∘φ and scheme maps p,q,r with q≫p=r, the direct δ equals localized scalar reassociation, then δ for ψ on the extended pair, then Lq*(δ for φ), then the fixed perfectHomComposition comparison [lem-pc-perfect-hom-transport] and equality transport. This equality holds at each label. No target objects P,Q, bottom-model identifications, base-change diagram, cocone or propagated object isomorphisms occur in this statement. Extension preserves K-flatness [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars]; all data in the coordinate record are supplied, and no witness is chosen in a definition.

proof.text: Construct the canonical natural family of chart object comparisons on the full category of the two labelled K-flat models. Its two components are explicitly the chart object comparisons.

Apply the one-model chart cocycle first to M and then to N. Rewrite the family components at true and false by their defining equalities and simplify cond. This gives the two required composition equations without changing the family or any supplied chart data.

The existing transport wrapper expands mapIso functoriality and the projection triangle. Naturality of the fixed composition isomorphism moves each bottom identification through it. Apply the two just-proved component equations to obtain AffineComparisonTransportTriangle; this original proof is retained.
